issues.legal_issue: The expression covering a company whose business consists mainly in holding investments includes a company whose principal income comes from house property that it holds and leases.
material_facts: The company’s objects included purchasing land and buildings and letting them out for consideration.
During the relevant years, the company invested money in house properties and derived its major income from those properties, which it leased to tenants.
The dispute concerned whether the company fell within the investment-holding category for the additional super-tax regime applicable to undistributed profits.
issues.conclusion: The company fell within the expression because its principal income was derived from house properties that it leased out. The High Court was correct, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 23A(1) and Explanation 2(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, “investment” was not defined and was not required to bear the restricted technical meaning of “investment companies” under section 87(f) of the Indian Companies Act, 1913, or section 372(11) of the Companies Act, 1956. The legislative history showed that the legislature intended a wider scope, so the expression was to be understood in its ordinary popular business sense. The Court followed Commissioner of Sales Tax, M.P., Indore v. Jaswant Singh Charan Singh and relied on Commissioner of Income Tax v. Vazir Sultan & Sons for the use of English authorities on analogous provisions. It referred to Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Gas Lighting Improvement Co. Ltd., Inland Revenue Commissioners v. Desoutter Bros Ltd., Inland Revenue Commissioners v. Broadway Car Co. (Wimbledon) Ltd., Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Tootal Broadhurst Lee Co. Ltd., and Inland Revenue Commissioners v. Rolls-Royce Ltd. The Court distinguished Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat v. Distributors (Baroda) P. Ltd. as turning on its particular facts. It also noted that the dictionary meaning of “investment companies” supported the same result.

predicates.company_additional_tax_classification_ca: The proceeding concerns whether a company falls within a category used to determine additional tax on undistributed profits.
predicates.principal_income_from_leased_property: The company holds property, leases it to others, and derives its principal income from that property.

issues.definition: When a company-tax classification proceeding concerns a company whose principal income comes from property it holds and leases, the company falls within the investment-holding category.
